mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in real GDP by more than 1% over the last six months signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3% in the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP decreases by more than 0.5% and retail and food services sales increase by more than 1% over the last month, it signals a shift in consumer spending patterns that historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decrease > 0.5% and RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 decreases and RSAFS increases on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
